title: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation / Stretch Extinction Using Counterflow Flames

sources.title: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation / Stretch Extinction Using Counterflow Flames

key_findings: The warm flame has a double reaction zone structure and plays a critical role in the transition between cool flames and hot flames.
At elevated pressures, the flammable region of warm flames and cool flames expands due to the increase in low-temperature and intermediate-temperature reactivity with pressure.
fields.earth_applications: Understanding near-limit flame dynamics and providing guidance for experimental observation of different flame regimes.

conditions.label: FLEX flight conditions
evidence: Since many real engines operate in the 20-40 atm pressure range, therefore, cool flames and warm flames are relevant and important flame regimes for high-pressure near-limit combustion applications.
